question: An employee keeps a connector to a shared team drive in place after moving to a completely different department. What is the greatest concern?
options: A) The drive's files are duplicated into the employee's own personal account and count against their storage.
B) Claude keeps reaching material the person no longer needs, so access is broader than their current role.
C) The organisation's owner is blocked from enabling any further connectors until this one is removed.
D) The connector stops working entirely, so any project relying on it returns an error to every member.
correct_answers: B) Claude keeps reaching material the person no longer needs, so access is broader than their current role.
explanations: Connectors do not copy files into the individual's own storage.
Correct. A connection left in place after a role change quietly extends access beyond what the job now requires.
One connection does not prevent others from being enabled.
A department move does not by itself break a connector.
